gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

gaps.sentence: The two designs are quite ___ from each other.
gaps.explanation: 'Different from' — the adjective is required after 'quite'.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: The ___ cost was much higher than the estimate.
gaps.explanation: 'Actual' means real or existing in fact; 'current' means belonging to the present time.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.
___ at this old photo — isn't it amazing?
gaps.explanation: 'Look at' means to direct your eyes towards something; the other verbs cannot be followed by 'at' here.

gaps.sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
gaps.explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.
